title: dev/engineering/registry.yaml (strict subset)
description: Descriptive schema for the hand-maintained registry. Enforcement is hand-rolled inside scripts/gen-current-state.mjs so that it runs with no node_modules; that code is authoritative and this file is kept aligned with it field by field. Where the two disagree the validator wins, and the disagreement is a defect in this file. Three things are enforced that a draft-07 reader cannot see: a repeated key inside one mapping, a repeated TOP-LEVEL key (including a second entries:), and this closed field set itself (REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_FIELD). Claim binding rules (CLAIM_TIER_*, MERGED_CLAIM_*, RELEASE_CLAIM_*) are cross-field and live only in the validator.

x-generated-view-mirror._note: Not part of the registry document: this file is also where the generated view's read-only mirror of graph.yaml#current_contract is documented, because that mirror is emitted by the same validator and has to be pinned against it. Enforcement lives in scripts/gen-current-state.mjs (LEGACY_MIRROR_KEYS + checkLegacyMirror): the list below and that constant must name the same fields in the same order, and a disagreement is a finding, not a documentation nit. Values are copied verbatim from the graph block -- the mirror never resolves them, so `baseline` stays the frozen recorded SHA and `matrix` stays a path rather than becoming a live tool table.

verified_tier.description: verification responsibility and coverage of this claim: C1 Adapter-local verification, C2 real-Host integration verification at a fixed SHA, C3 final verification of a fixed candidate. Levels are not machines -- CI can execute C1. Not the same vocabulary as verification_status.

x-invariants.INV-EB-0009: the four status fields are independent; no value of one field implies a value of another
x-invariants.FAKE_VERIFICATION: verification_status starting with 'verified' requires at least one existing path in verification_artifacts; otherwise generation is refused
x-invariants.NO_WALL_CLOCK: the generated view contains no wall-clock timestamp, so --check is byte-reproducible for identical inputs
x-invariants.DUPLICATE_KEY: a repeated key in one mapping, or a repeated top-level key such as a second entries:, is refused rather than last-write-wins
x-invariants.CLOSED_FIELDS: any entry field outside the list above is refused (REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_FIELD), which is what additionalProperties:false means in practice
